title: Flattening by an admissible blowup (Raynaud--Gruson)
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme which is quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism], let $U\subseteq T$ be a quasi-compact open subscheme, and let $g:W\to T$ be a morphism of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] which is quasi-separated [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism] and whose restriction $g^{-1}(U)\to U$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Then there is a quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_T$ of finite type with $\mathcal I|_U=\mathcal O_U$ (a $U$-admissible blowup centre [def-nagata-admissible-blowup]) such that, writing $\pi:T'=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(T)\to T$ for its blowup [def-nagata-global-blowup], the strict transform $W'\subseteq W\times_TT'$ of $W$ [def-nagata-strict-transform], namely the scheme-theoretic closure in $W\times_TT'$ [def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-image] of the open subscheme lying over $T\setminus V(\mathcal I)$, is flat over $T'$ and of finite presentation over $T'$, that is, locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact and quasi-separated.

source.place: Tag 081R, lemma-flat-after-blowing-up; strict transform as in literature/stacks-project/divisors.tex Tag 080D, definition-strict-transform. Cited by literature/illusie-laszlo-orgogozo-travaux-de-gabber_arXiv-1207.3648.pdf, Expose X, proof of Theorem 3.4, Step 2 (Raynaud-Gruson 5.7.9).

proof.text: Because $g:W\to T$ is of finite type, every affine open of $T$ has inverse image covered by finitely many affine opens of $W$; quasi-compactness of $T$ therefore gives a finite affine open cover $W=\bigcup_{i=1}^r W_i$. Flatness and local finite presentation are local on the source, so it is enough to construct, for each $W_i$, a $U$-admissible blowup on which the strict transform of $W_i$ is flat and of finite presentation. The hypotheses used here are exactly the conventions that “of finite type” means quasi-compact and locally of finite type, and that $g$ is quasi-separated.

source.place: Tag 081R, proof: finite affine covering and locality of flatness and finite presentation

proof.text: Fix an affine piece $W_i$. Its morphism to $T$ is locally of finite type, so [lemma-nagata-quasi-affine-immersion-affine-space-exists] gives an immersion into $\mathbb A_T^{n_i}$. Choose a quasi-compact open neighbourhood $V_i$ of its image on which it is a closed immersion $j_i:W_i\hookrightarrow V_i$. Such a neighbourhood exists by the definition of immersion and quasi-compactness of $W_i$. On every affine open $\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq V_i$, the inverse image is $\operatorname{Spec}(B/J)$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]; thus $\mathcal F_i=(j_i)_*\mathcal O_{W_i}$ is locally $\widetilde{B/J}$, a cyclic module, hence quasi-coherent and of finite type [pqf-def-coherent]. The scheme $V_i$ is quasi-compact and locally of finite presentation over $T$, since it is open in a finite-dimensional relative affine space.

source.place: Tag 081R, affine immersion and choice of V

proof.text: Check finite presentation of $\mathcal F_i$ over $U$. On affine charts over $\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq U$, write $\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq V_{i,U}$ and $j_i^{-1}(\operatorname{Spec}B)=\operatorname{Spec}A$, with $A=B/J$. Here $B$ is of finite type over $R$ and $A$ is of finite presentation over $R$, because $W_U\to U$ is locally of finite presentation. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-over-finite-type-algebra], $A$ is finitely presented over $B$ (the affine argument for Morphisms 02FV). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-surjection-kernel-fg] with coefficient ring $B$ and zero polynomial variables: $J=(a_1,\ldots,a_s)$. The exact sequence $B^s\xrightarrow{(a_1,\ldots,a_s)}B\to B/J\to0$, sheafified on this chart, is a finite module presentation [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation]. This explicitly proves the required finite-presentation pushforward assertion in this closed-immersion case. At image points the stalk of $\mathcal F_i$ equals the stalk of $\mathcal O_{W_i}$; outside the closed image it is zero. The hypothesis of flatness over $U$ therefore says exactly that these stalks are flat over the corresponding local rings of $U$.

source.place: Tag 081R, hypotheses for theorem-flatten-module; morphisms.tex Tag 02FV and algebra.tex Tag 00F4 (4), Tag 00R2

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-flattening-module-by-admissible-blowup] to $V_i\to T$, $\mathcal F_i$, and $U$. The base is qcqs, $V_i$ is quasi-compact and locally of finite presentation, $\mathcal F_i$ is finite type, and its restriction over $U$ is finitely presented and flat by the preceding steps. This gives a $U$-admissible blowup $b_i:T_i\to T$ with the module strict transform $\mathcal F_i^b$ [def-trf-module-strict-transform] flat over $T_i$ and finitely presented over $V_i\times_TT_i$.

Apply [lem-trf-strict-transform-affine-pushforward] to the affine morphism $j_i$ and $\mathcal O_{W_i}$. By [def-trf-module-strict-transform], the strict transform of $\mathcal O_{W_i}$ is the structure sheaf of the scheme strict transform $W_i^b$, pushed forward into $W_i\times_TT_i$: both are the quotient of the structure sheaf by sections supported on the exceptional inverse image. Indeed, the ideal of the scheme-theoretic closure is the kernel of restriction to the complementary open, precisely those supported sections [def-nagata-strict-transform]. Consequently the affine-pushforward comparison identifies $\mathcal F_i^b$ with $(j_i^b)_*\mathcal O_{W_i^b}$, where $j_i^b:W_i^b\hookrightarrow V_i\times_TT_i$ is a closed immersion. We use this comparison of modules, rather than the ambient-closed comparison of schemes.

Flatness of the identified module means, on the closed image, flatness of the identical stalks of $\mathcal O_{W_i^b}$ over $T_i$, hence $W_i^b\to T_i$ is flat. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-kernel-surjection-finite-type] to the surjection $\mathcal O_{V_i\times_TT_i}\to(j_i^b)_*\mathcal O_{W_i^b}$. Its kernel is locally generated by finitely many sections. Thus locally $W_i^b$ is cut out by finitely many equations in $V_i\times_TT_i$, which is locally of finite presentation over $T_i$. On affine charts, a finitely presented base algebra followed by a quotient by finitely many equations is finitely presented, by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-base-change-composition]. Therefore $W_i^b\to T_i$ is locally of finite presentation.

Choose the finite-type centre ideals $\mathcal I_i$ of $b_i$ and put $\mathcal I=\prod_i\mathcal I_i$, $T^b=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(T)$. The product is finite type and restricts to the unit ideal on $U$, so this is $U$-admissible [def-nagata-admissible-blowup]. For fixed $i$, put $\mathcal J_i=\prod_{k\ne i}\mathcal I_k$. The product-blowup theorem [thm-nagata-blowup-product-ideal], with the iterated blowup of [def-nagata-blowup-product-comparison], identifies $T^b\to T_i$ with the blowup of the extended ideal $\mathcal J_i\mathcal O_{T_i}$. In particular it is a $U$-admissible blowup, not merely a morphism dominating $T_i$. The support condition for composition is also satisfied: off $V(\mathcal I_i)$ the map $b_i$ is an isomorphism (apply the cited open-complement lemma with preserved open $T\setminus V(\mathcal I_i)$), so the image of $V(\mathcal J_i\mathcal O_{T_i})$ there is $V(\mathcal J_i)\setminus V(\mathcal I_i)$; over $V(\mathcal I_i)$ it adds nothing to the union. Hence $V(\mathcal I)=V(\mathcal I_i)\cup b_i(V(\mathcal J_i\mathcal O_{T_i}))$.

source.place: Tag 081R, finite affine-cover reduction; divisors.tex Tags 080A, 080N

proof.text: For each $i$, apply [lem-trf-strict-transform-composition] with $S=T$, $S_1=T_i$, $S_2=T^b$, $Z=V(\mathcal I_i)$, $Z_1=V(\mathcal J_i\mathcal O_{T_i})$, and $Y=V(\mathcal I)$. The previous step supplies both the blowup factorization and its support equality. It follows that the strict transform of $W_i$ for the single centre $\mathcal I$ agrees with the strict transform of $W_i^b\to T_i$ for the centre $\mathcal J_i\mathcal O_{T_i}$.

source.place: Tag 081R, reduction using remark-successive-blowups; divisors.tex Tag 080I (2)

proof.text: Since $W_i^b\to T_i$ is flat, its strict transform for the further blowup equals its base change to $T^b$: [thm-nagata-strict-transform-is-blowup] identifies that strict transform with the blowup of $W_i^b$ in the extended centre, and [thm-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change] identifies the latter with $W_i^b\times_{T_i}T^b$ by the comparison of [def-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change-map]. Flatness of this base change follows from [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change]; local finite presentation follows chartwise from the base-change clause of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-base-change-composition]. Thus every strict transform of $W_i$ on $T^b$ is flat and locally of finite presentation. This proves the persistence assertion using flatness at all points; it does not assume that the original open $U$ was dense in $T$.

source.place: Tag 081R and remark-successive-blowups; divisors.tex Tags 080E and flat-base-change comparison (equivalently 080F (1))

proof.text: The strict transform $W'$ of $W$ is covered by the strict transforms of the finite affine opens $W_i$. Flatness and local finite presentation are local on the source, hence $W'\to T'$ has both properties. Since $W\to T$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, its base change $W\times_TT'\to T'$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]; the closed immersion $W'\hookrightarrow W\times_TT'$ is affine, hence quasi-compact and separated, and composing gives that $W'\to T'$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Consequently $W'\to T'$ is of finite presentation, completing the construction of the required $U$-admissible blowup.
